Definition: from G459; illegality, i.e. violation of law or (genitive case) wickedness:--iniquity, X transgress(-ion of) the law, unrighteousness.
BiblicalUsage: Lawlessness is sin's own name: John says sin is the transgression of the law, Jesus will tell the workers of iniquity to depart from Him, and Paul says the mystery of iniquity already works in the world. The word names life lived as if God's law did not exist.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lawlessness is not freedom but rebellion with the label torn off: a life that answers to no law but its own. John names it plainly, sin is the transgression of the law, and I hold that the cure is not a lighter law but a new heart that loves the law it once broke.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
